module_title: Post-LPG Reforms: Inclusive and Sustainable Growth (8th to 12th)
introduction: Post-1991, India moved from 'Imperative Planning' (Government-led) to 'Indicative Planning' (Market-led), focusing more on human development and sustainability.

core_concepts.title: Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997)
core_concepts.description: Known as the 'Rao-Manmohan Model'. It was the first plan post-LPG reforms. The main focus shifted to 'Human Resource Development' (Education, Health). It achieved a stellar growth rate of 6.8%.

core_concepts.title: Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-2012)
core_concepts.description: Theme: 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'. Fact: This plan recorded the 'Highest Growth Rate' (approx. 8%) compared to all other plans.

core_concepts.title: Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012-2017)
core_concepts.description: This was India’s 'Last' Five-Year Plan. Theme: 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth'. After this, the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog.

core_concepts.title: Indicative Planning
core_concepts.description: After the 8th Plan, the state’s role became that of a facilitator rather than a controller. The market was given the lead, and the government only 'indicated' the direction of growth.

important_entities.name: Hindu Rate of Growth
important_entities.significance: A term used mockingly to describe the slow growth rate (3.5%) of the Indian economy from the 1950s to the 1980s. Post-1991 plans finally buried this term.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: UPSC/PCS Trap: 11th Plan Theme: 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth'. 12th Plan Theme: 'Faster, More Inclusive and *Sustainable* Growth'. The word 'Sustainable' is the key differentiator.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Coming after the 1991 crisis, the 8th plan put 'Humans' (Education/Health) at the center.

exam_strategy_tips: Always check the growth achieved. The 11th Plan was the 'most successful' in terms of raw percentage growth (8%).
